text:
The Avalanche come to Montreal without both of their superstars. Nathan MacKinnon (30 points in 20 games) and Cale Makar (23 in 19) are out with lower-body injuries, and the Denver Post's Corey Masisak wrote that it sounds like at least a month for MacKinnon; ESPN's estimates are Dec 12 for him and Nov 28 for Makar. At the morning skate, Masisak posted a new first power play of Devon Toews, Nazem Kadri, Hughes, Martin Necas and Artturi Lehkonen. Brent Burns, next in line for Makar's minutes, plays his 1,600th NHL game.

The Canadiens have points in twelve straight (9-0-3), and they've done it on even terms: 50% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in that run, so this is a team grinding out results more than overwhelming anyone. They're shorthanded too. Ivan Demidov (ankle) is on injured reserve, with Cole Caufield taking his spot beside Juraj Slafkovský and Alex Newhook, and Daily Faceoff reported Chris Kreider is out six to eight weeks. Caufield carries a five-game point streak into it; Slafkovský has no goals in ten games on 3.3 expected.

The goaltending gap is the number to watch. Jakub Dobes is confirmed for Montreal (Karine Hains of The Hockey News posted "Dobes in"), and he has had a rough start: .846 and 6.0 goals allowed above expected after saving 17.3 more than expected last season. Mackenzie Blackwood, our projected starter for Colorado, is at +1.0. Our playoff model puts the Avalanche at 96% and the Canadiens at 73%.

We have two sleepers on the Colorado side. Jaden Schwartz, a third-liner at about 12:49 a night, has 1.9 expected goals in his last 10 games, better than 70% of depth forwards; we have him at 18% to score and 39% for a point. Nazem Kadri, next in line for MacKinnon's minutes by our depth chart, is at 58% for a point against his season pace of 52%, because his line creates 4.29 expected goals per 60 and Montreal allows the 8th-most.
headline: Avalanche without MacKinnon and Makar in Montreal
